name: Casey Hunter
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember hearing the winch the day my partner lost her grip.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Casey takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I am the fishing partner who was there that day. I want the client to know she can tell as much or little as she likes.
appearance: Casey is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a small enamel bird on the lapel, Casey turns fully toward the person speaking when listening.
personality: Casey admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Casey learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To let the former partner choose what to tell about the accident.
family: Lena Roth is Casey’s cousin. Casey asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Lena remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The sandwich board*, Lena says, “I promised the owner her business would survive.”
connections: Riley Evans. The original fishing partner meets a second worker who will model an injury on separate terms. Also in the story is Duncan Stahl (former crewmate).

reactions.response: Casey asks the model whether the original permission covers the scar.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Casey stays where both neighbors can hear a familiar voice and gets news from the caretaker.
